subject: Finalizing closure criteria and tiebreak for Kellan Myers — feedback and anchors
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: ExternalRecruiting <externalrecruiting@hirewell.co>
Date: Fri, 2 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Finalizing closure criteria and tiebreak for Kellan Myers — feedback and anchors

Team —

Thanks again for taking the time with Kellan yesterday. I pulled together the attachments (resume + consolidated scorecard template) and a short list of closure criteria we discussed live. We need to lock this by EOD PST so recruiting can extend an offer if we hit the bar.

Quick asks:
- Please open the attached scorecard-Kellan-Myers.csv and add your numeric scores (1–5) and one-line rationale by 5:00pm PT today. If you have a hard +/– hire call, write that in the "recommendation" column.
- If you are on the fence, add a single example of observed behavior that would push you to a hire. Avoid long prose — one bullet is fine.
- If we end up with a split vote, our agreed tiebreak order is: (1) technical breadth on infra-serving patterns; (2) capacity to onboard quickly (first 30/60/90 plan); (3) culture/team fit.

Anchor criteria (for consistent scoring):
- System design at scale (30%): clarity of tradeoffs, latency/cost reasoning.
- Debugging & incident practice (25%): ownership examples and runbook thinking.
- ML/infra product sense (20%): shipping tradeoffs and downstream impact.
- Communication & collaboration (15%): cross-team work and clarity.
- Signals & growth potential (10%)

Attachments: Kellan_Myers_resume.pdf, scorecard-Kellan-Myers.csv

If anyone wants a 15-min quick call to align on anchors, say so now and I’ll grab a slot. Otherwise I’ll consolidate everything and post a final note to recruiting.

Thanks —
Mina
Mina Haddad
Hiring Manager, Infra Serving
Redwood Inference

I filled the scorecard and attached a short note (marissa-notes.pdf) with two points I want to highlight:
- Strength: Kellan has clear instincts around KV cache management and proposed a reasonable fallback strategy for cold-starts.
- Risk: His latency-cost tradeoff examples were lighter on numbers — I'd like to see a quick follow-up on expected throughput for the proposed design (QPS targets).

My recommendation: +1 hire, contingent on a 30-min check to validate throughput estimates (can be async with an exercise).

- Jonas Weber: +1 hire
